title: Massachusetts treats the do-not-fill-before date as the date of issuance of a multiple Schedule II prescription
subtopic: Multiple Schedule II prescriptions and the Massachusetts date of issuance
rule_summary: A Board of Registration in Medicine guideline adopted on October 22, 2008, published on mass.gov as Appendix C, 2007-01 Joint Policy Regarding Issuance of Multiple Prescriptions for Schedule II Controlled Substances, records that the Massachusetts Drug Control Program and the Board of Pharmacy have determined that issuing multiple Schedule II prescriptions in accordance with the requirements of the amended federal regulation is permissible under M.G.L. c. 94C, and that the Board of Registration in Medicine concurs with their Joint Policy. It states that the 'Date of Issuance' referred to in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23 shall be the 'Do Not Fill Before' date indicated by the prescriber, that the 'date written' under s. 23 shall be the date the prescription was written and signed by the prescriber, and that accordingly each written prescription will become invalid thirty days after its date of issuance. It also reports DEA's interpretation of the federal provision that no pharmacist may fill such a prescription before the indicated date: no verbal modifications can be made to the earliest date on which the Schedule II prescription may be filled. The Board of Registration in Pharmacy's December 2025 newsletter states that federal law allows prescribers to issue multiple Schedule II prescriptions (up to a 90-day supply) using the date of issuance (date written) and a 'do not fill before' date; that since prescriptions may not be post-dated, the clock would start from the later 'do not fill before' date (if there is one); and that, if issued by a Massachusetts prescriber, Schedule II prescriptions are valid for 30 days from the date of issuance or the 'do not fill before' date, as applicable.
exam_relevance: Tests how the Massachusetts 30-day validity of a Schedule II prescription applies to the later prescriptions of a federal multiple-prescription set: the Massachusetts guidance measures it from the prescriber's do-not-fill-before date, while the date written remains the date the prescription was written and signed.

numeric_facts.fact: validity of a Massachusetts prescriber's Schedule II prescription carrying a do-not-fill-before date
numeric_facts.conditions: measured from the do-not-fill-before date, which the guidance treats as the date of issuance under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23

common_confusions: For a prescription carrying a do-not-fill-before date, the guidance measures the 30 days from that date, not from the date written.
The date written remains the date the prescription was written and signed by the prescriber.
verification_notes: Read the Appendix C 2007-01 guideline document on mass.gov and the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's December 2025 newsletter article Multiple Schedule II Prescriptions on 2026-09-14. The guideline's second part, on a sixty-day supply of certain stimulants, reflects the earlier text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23(d) and is not carried by this rule.
